summary: GiftCookie is a specialized kind of Cookie for the bakery's gift orders. It inherits everything an ordinary cookie can do and adds its own gift-wrapping steps: boxing, ribbon, and a note.

lines.text: The extends keyword makes GiftCookie a Cookie, so it already knows how to be mixed and baked; only the gift-specific responsibilities need to be written here.
A subclass constructor hands the flavor up to the Cookie constructor so the inherited part of the object is set up properly before any gift logic runs.
This is the one public door into the gift-wrapping process, and the rest of the bakery application can only ask for the whole process, never for individual steps.

lines.code: System.out.println("Packaged " + getFlavor() + " cookie in a box.");
lines.text: getFlavor() is not defined in this file; it is inherited from Cookie, which is why GiftCookie will not compile unless the Cookie class is available too.

Marking the helper steps private is encapsulation in practice: GiftCookie keeps control of how gift wrapping is done and in what order, so no other code can tie the ribbon before the cookie is in the box.
